chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: How Le Ruban Bleu ran: acts, Chittison and the house trio
summary: The club's schedule of acts, Herman Chittison's group with Dave Barber and Sedric Wallace, and why she stayed six years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, can I go back to the Le Ruban Bleu?
Yes.
Earlier on in the interviewing you mentioned the, this innovation that they introduced there, of having a sequence of that, I guess. Can you tell us how that developed?

Well, the club opened at night. The first act went on at nine o'clock. And the room was open till four o'clock in the morning. But what Jacoby did, instead of, well they had a trio there for one thing.

Was that the Herman Chittison? --the house band?
Yes, that was Herman Chittison.
And at that time he had Dave Barber with him and Sedric Wallace. Sedric Wallace was originally with Fats Waller.
And the leader of the record you did.

Yeah. But they would put an act on at a certain hour and then there would be a lull, not exactly a lull because then the trio would play, and then another act, the trio, another act. And no act, they had four acts during the course of the evening and no act went on twice a night. You just got up there and did your whole repertoire, whatever you wanted to do. And I enjoyed that because it gave me a chance to get away from sticking to things like 'Loch Lomond'. I did what was currently popular and also allot of standards. And I felt a little freer that way. I had more time to do the things that I wanted to do. And of course, working with Herman Chittison was a dream.
I'm sure.
I really, the reason I stayed in the Le Ruban Bleu for six years because Herman wouldn't

go out on the road. I would like to have traveled with him, you know, doing lounges or some of the hotels and things like that but he didn't want to leave New York so I stayed at the Le Ruban Bleu. And the first time I went down to the Village Vanguard to work they had . . .
That would have been after the war?
Yeah, after the war. Sure, because I was at the Le Ruban Bleu for six years.
How many weeks a year would you have played that?
Well, I worked at the Le Ruban Bleu, they had a season, like you went in in June - I mean you went in in September and you stayed, the room was open till June.
I see.

I stayed there, I was year round when I was there. However, in the meantime they would engage different acts at different times. I think the initial engagement was like four weeks.
